control_implications.headline: Microsoft Store application delivers Vinci RAT remote access trojan
control_implications.significance: Compromise of a Microsoft Store application to deliver malware indicates that application vetting and supply chain controls may not prevent malicious code distribution through trusted platforms. paragraphs.text: Active exploitation of critical vulnerabilities in Drupal core, the Cacti network monitoring platform, US Air Force cloud infrastructure, and government visa systems demonstrates that vulnerability management and monitoring controls must address both known exploited flaws and zero-day threats across diverse technology stacks.

The addition of Mitel MiCollab vulnerabilities to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and the compromise of a Microsoft Store application to deliver a remote access trojan indicate that third-party risk assurance and application vetting controls require reinforcement to address supply chain exploitation.
